name: ct
description: Generic container types. Provides Vec, HashMap, Set, Queue, Deque, and Pair.

structs.name: Deque
structs.description: Double-ended queue with elements of type T.  Fields:   data - Pointer to circular buffer   head - Index of front element   tail - Index after last element   len  - Number of elements   cap  - Buffer capacity

structs.name: Map
structs.description: Hash map with string keys and values of type V.  Fields:   keys   - Array of string key pointers   values - Array of V values   states - Array of slot states (0=empty, 1=occupied, 2=deleted)   len    - Number of entries   cap    - Allocated capacity

structs.name: Pair
structs.description: Pair<T, U> - A Generic Two-Element Tuple ========================================  Pair holds two values of potentially different types. Useful for returning multiple values or key-value associations.  ## Creating a Pair      Pair<i64, str> { first = 42 second = "hello" } -> p  ## Accessing Elements      p <<first -> key     p <<second -> value  ## Unpacking Both Elements      p unpack -> a -> b A pair of two values.  Fields:   first  - The first element of type T   second - The second element of type U

structs.name: Queue
structs.description: FIFO Queue with elements of type T.  Fields:   data - Pointer to circular buffer   head - Index of front element   tail - Index after last element   len  - Number of elements   cap  - Buffer capacity

structs.name: Set
structs.description: Set of unique string elements.  Fields:   keys   - Array of string key pointers   states - Array of slot states (0=empty, 1=occupied, 2=deleted)   len    - Number of elements   cap    - Allocated capacity

structs.name: Vec
structs.description: Dynamic array (vector) structure.  Fields:   data - Pointer to contiguous element storage   len  - Current number of elements (0 to cap)   cap  - Allocated capacity in elements

functions.name: add
functions.description: Add an element to the set.  If the element already exists, the set is unchanged. Returns the updated set which must be captured.  Example:     s "alice" add! -> s  Stack: (s key -- s2)

functions.name: capacity
functions.description: Get the allocated capacity.  Capacity is always >= length. The vector can hold up to 'capacity' elements before needing to reallocate.  Example:     v capacity -> cap  Stack: (v -- n)

functions.name: contains
functions.description: Check if an element exists in the set.  Example:     s "alice" contains if { "found!" print nl }  Stack: (s key -- exists)

functions.name: dequeue
functions.description: Remove and return the front element.  Returns error if queue is empty. Returns the value and updated queue.  Example:     q dequeue! -> q -> val  Stack: (q -- val q2)

functions.name: enqueue
functions.description: Add an element to the back of the queue.  Returns the updated queue which must be captured.  Example:     q 42 enqueue! -> q  Stack: (q val -- q2)

functions.name: first
functions.description: Get the first element of a pair.  Example:     p first -> a  Stack: (p -- a)

functions.name: get
functions.description: Get the value for a key.  Returns an error if the key is not found.  Example:     m "alice" get! -> age  Stack: (m key -- value)

functions.name: get
functions.description: Get element at index.  Panics if index is out of bounds (< 0 or >= len).  Example:     v 0 get! -> first  Stack: (v idx -- elem)

functions.name: has
functions.description: Check if a key exists in the map.  Example:     m "alice" has if { "found!" print nl }  Stack: (m key -- exists)

functions.name: insert
functions.description: Insert a key-value pair into the map.  If the key already exists, the value is updated. Returns the updated map which must be captured.  Example:     m "alice" 42 insert! -> m  Stack: (m key value -- m2)

functions.name: is_empty
functions.description: Check if the deque is empty.  Stack: (d -- bool)

functions.name: is_empty
functions.description: Check if the map is empty.  Example:     m is_empty if { "empty!" print nl }  Stack: (m -- bool)

functions.name: is_empty
functions.description: Check if the queue is empty.  Stack: (q -- bool)

functions.name: is_empty
functions.description: Check if the set is empty.  Example:     s is_empty if { "empty!" print nl }  Stack: (s -- bool)

functions.name: is_empty
functions.description: Check if the vector is empty (length == 0).  Example:     v is_empty if { "empty!" print nl }  Stack: (v -- bool)

functions.name: length
functions.description: Get the number of elements.  Stack: (d -- n)

functions.name: length
functions.description: Get the number of entries in the map.  Example:     m length -> n  Stack: (m -- n)

functions.name: length
functions.description: Get the number of elements in the queue.  Stack: (q -- n)

functions.name: length
functions.description: Get the number of elements in the set.  Example:     s length -> n  Stack: (s -- n)

functions.name: length
functions.description: Get the number of elements in the vector.  Example:     v length -> n  Stack: (v -- n)

functions.name: peek_back
functions.description: View the back element without removing it.  Stack: (d -- val)

functions.name: peek_front
functions.description: View the front element without removing it.  Stack: (d -- val)

functions.name: peek
functions.description: View the front element without removing it.  Returns error if queue is empty.  Example:     q peek! -> val  Stack: (q -- val)

functions.name: pop_back
functions.description: Remove and return the back element.  Example:     d pop_back! -> d -> val  Stack: (d -- val d2)

functions.name: pop_front
functions.description: Remove and return the front element.  Example:     d pop_front! -> d -> val  Stack: (d -- val d2)

functions.name: pop
functions.description: Pop and return the last element.  Panics if the vector is empty. Returns both the element and the updated vector.  Example:     v pop! -> v -> elem  Stack: (v -- elem v2)

functions.name: push_back
functions.description: Push an element to the back.  Example:     d 42 push_back! -> d  Stack: (d val -- d2)

functions.name: push_front
functions.description: Push an element to the front.  Example:     d 42 push_front! -> d  Stack: (d val -- d2)

functions.name: push
functions.description: Push an element to the end of the vector.  Automatically grows capacity when full (doubles size, starting at 8). Returns the updated vector which must be captured.  Example:     v 42 push! -> v  Stack: (v elem -- v2)

functions.name: release
functions.description: Free the deque's memory.  Stack: (d --)

functions.name: release
functions.description: Free the map's memory.  IMPORTANT: Always call this when done with a map to prevent memory leaks. After calling release, the map should not be used.  Example:     m release  Stack: (m --)

functions.name: release
functions.description: Free the queue's memory.  Stack: (q --)

functions.name: release
functions.description: Free the set's memory.  IMPORTANT: Always call this when done with a set to prevent memory leaks.  Example:     s release  Stack: (s --)

functions.name: release
functions.description: Free the vector's memory.  IMPORTANT: Always call this when done with a vector to prevent memory leaks. After calling release, the vector should not be used.  Example:     v release  Stack: (v --)

functions.name: remove
functions.description: Remove a key from the map.  Returns error if the key is not found. Returns the updated map which must be captured.  Example:     m "alice" remove! -> m  Stack: (m key -- m2)

functions.name: remove
functions.description: Remove an element from the set.  Returns error if the element is not found. Returns the updated set which must be captured.  Example:     s "alice" remove! -> s  Stack: (s key -- s2)

functions.name: reset
functions.description: Remove all elements, keeping allocated capacity.  Useful for reusing a vector without reallocating.  Example:     v reset -> v  Stack: (v -- v2)

functions.name: second
functions.description: Get the second element of a pair.  Example:     p second -> b  Stack: (p -- b)

functions.name: set
functions.description: Set element at index.  Panics if index is out of bounds (< 0 or >= len). Returns the updated vector which must be captured.  Example:     v 0 100 set! -> v  Stack: (v idx elem -- v2)

functions.name: unpack
functions.description: Unpack a pair onto the stack.  Returns both elements: first is deeper, second on top.  Example:     p unpack -> first_val -> second_val  Stack: (p -- a b)
